acts.desc: Producer Chana Joffe-Walt fills in for Ira Glass this week. We hear from a person you don’t normally hear from in these kinds of stories — the partner of a man who has been accused of sexual harassment. She finds herself thinking about an old memory, and reconsidering things she’d come to think of as normal. (7 1/2 minutes.)
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Growing up, Deanna is told that relationships with men won’t be easy: that men are dumb and she’ll have to make sense of things for them. Throughout her twenties, this proves true. So she’s surprised when she meets a man who’s different — Don.
acts.title: Deanna

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Alternet editors try to figure out what to make of Deanna’s odd behavior at an all-staff dinner.
acts.title: The Dinner

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: When Onnesha asks Don for a raise, he asks her a weird question. One that brings to mind a realization Onnesha had as a thirteen-year-old at the swimming pool.
acts.title: Onnesha

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Don’s behavior grows increasingly troubling to Deanna.
acts.title: The Cliff

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Tana is clear on how to deal with Don. She’s the cool girl, he’s the flirty boss. And then Don does something that seems out of bounds. (14 1/2 minutes)
acts.title: Tana

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: Kristen has no trouble naming what’s going on with Don: sexual harassment. She’s the first Alternet employee angry enough to try to do something about it. (16 1/2 minutes)
acts.title: Kristen

acts.label: Act Seven
acts.desc: We return to Vivian, Don’s partner, who reflects on how to incorporate some new information into the story of her own relationship with him.
acts.title: Vivian
